correctness.rationale: Headline claim: R(n)=max rainbow ordered Schur triples over 3-colorings of [1,n] for n=1..12 equals 0,0,2,4,6,8,12,14,18,22,28,30 with labeled-optimum counts 3,9,6,6,12,12,6,24,30,6,6,66 and S3-class counts 1,2,1,1,2,2,1,4,5,1,1,11, plus c0-template counts 0,0,2,4,6,8,10,14,18,22,26,30. Auditor independently re-ran full 3^n labeled brute force (separate code path, set-based rainbow predicate) for every n<=12: all maxima, labeled-optimum counts, S3-canonical class counts, stored class-rep coverage/inequivalence, DRAFT per-n witnesses, and c0 recount reproduced exactly. T(n)=n(n-1)/2 verified triple-by-triple. c(1)=0 fixing in enumerate.py is exact for maxima by global S3 symmetry and cross-validated by full labeled recount (agreement on all 12 values). n=12 representatives in DRAFT match results.json byte-for-byte. Conventions (ordered triples, colors {0,1,2}) are explicit and consistent; boundary n=1 (T=0) and n=2 (R=0, 2 classes) handled correctly. Exactness is computational (exhaustive enumeration + independent replay), honestly described as such with no closed-form claim.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp: Parczyk-Spiegel arXiv:2410.22024 (v2, Apr 2026) proves only asymptotic bounds 0.4<=max rainbow fraction<=0.66364, conjectures 0.4 tight, and states the construction was found via small-n computations but publishes no exact R(n) table or extremal classes (verified in full-text HTML). Budden-Landman arXiv:2401.07357 defines RS_m(n)=minimum colors forcing a rainbow solution (different invariant); Cheng et al. arXiv:2005.14384 counts rainbow-free colorings (different objective). Koutschan-Wong arXiv:1904.01925 and OEIS A321195 cover only 2-color monochromatic minima (floor((n^2-4n+6)/11)), opposite objective and disjoint from 3-color rainbow maxima. Live OEIS queries 'rainbow Schur' and 'maximum rainbow triples' return No results, and live prefix query 0,0,2,4,6,8,12,14,18,22 returns No results (checked 2026-09-08), confirming no database record. The R(n) values, S3-extremal classes, and c0-gap at n=7,11 are therefore new, positive, and not mechanically implied by any prior.

value.rationale: Headline is a rigorously established exact invariant of a natural object independently worth retrieving: maximum rainbow-Schur count R(n) for 3-colorings of [1,n]. Object and invariant were motivated before computation by the Graham-Rodl-Rucinski / Erdos-Sos lineage and the Parczyk-Spiegel 2024 program with explicit 0.4-tightness conjecture; the values were not known and are not mechanically implied by the asymptotic bounds or the 2-color formula. The table is the first small-n benchmark for that conjecture (scope n<=12 sits just below Schur number S(3)=14, natural and human-checkable), and the c0-vs-optimum gaps at n=7 (10<12) and n=11 (26<28) give a concrete small-n caveat a future researcher testing tightness would need. Per the value standard, a narrow exact datum qualifies when motivated, unknown, and plausibly needed later; no general theorem, completed census beyond n=12, or downstream use is demanded. Certification strengthens but does not alone create value here.
